-- t3a DRAFT (owner: Research). NOT part of the suite: parked outside
-- tests/corpus/ — denominator stays 208 until ordered.
-- Sequencing: authored BEFORE M19 starts (drafts-first, Tier-3 edition).
-- Spans M19 (freelist/VACUUM) and M20 (overflow pages, blobs) — Default
-- may split the landing; prediction covers the whole file.
-- src: authored   tier: t3 (tranche a: storage-engine depth, observable halves)
-- Note: page cache (M18), ANALYZE (M21), covering/partial indexes (M22) are
-- invisible to this file by design — outcomes don't change when those work;
-- their evidence is plan-level/benchmark, per the "what the corpus cannot
-- observe" section of the conformance spec.
-- Overflow cases rely on a body longer than one 4096-byte page (MiniDB's
-- documented page size from M3), so the record crosses into overflow pages
-- on disk. The --directive: reopen phases force the disk path.

-- OVERFLOW: a row larger than one page survives a disk round trip.

CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, body TEXT);
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, '');
--directive: reopen
SELECT id, length(body) FROM t;

-- MULTI-ROW WRITES AFTER REOPEN: several 1KB rows written to a freshly
-- reopened file, read back in a third phase — post-reopen write path and
-- page allocation both exercised at moderate size.

CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, body TEXT);
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 'pad');
--directive: reopen
INSERT INTO t VALUES (2, '');
INSERT INTO t VALUES (3, '');
--directive: reopen
SELECT id, length(body) FROM t ORDER BY id;

-- WIDE ROW: many small columns (record-format width, not page overflow).

CREATE TABLE t (a INTEGER, b TEXT, c REAL, d TEXT, e INTEGER, f TEXT, g REAL, h TEXT);
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 'x', 1.5, 'y', 2, 'z', 2.5, 'w');
--directive: reopen
SELECT a, c, g FROM t;

-- VACUUM: deleted rows stay gone and survivors are unchanged after VACUUM.

CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, v TEXT);
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 'keep');
INSERT INTO t VALUES (2, 'drop');
INSERT INTO t VALUES (3, 'keep');
DELETE FROM t WHERE id = 2;
VACUUM;
SELECT id, v FROM t ORDER BY id;

-- VACUUM with an index present: the index survives and still serves.

CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, v TEXT);
CREATE INDEX idx_v ON t (v);
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 'a');
INSERT INTO t VALUES (2, 'b');
DELETE FROM t WHERE id = 1;
VACUUM;
SELECT id, v FROM t WHERE v = 'b';

-- VACUUM then reopen: the vacuumed state is what persists.

CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER);
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1);
INSERT INTO t VALUES (2);
DELETE FROM t WHERE id = 2;
VACUUM;
--directive: reopen
SELECT id FROM t;

-- SWING / likely owned gap: hex blob literal and its storage class.
-- SQLite: typeof(X'0102') = 'blob'. The ladder's M20 covers "large rows
-- and blobs"; if blob literals are unimplemented this fails and is owned.

SELECT typeof(X'0102');

-- SWING: blob round trip through a table + reopen — stored bytes are the
-- bytes, storage class 'blob' end to end.

CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, payload BLOB);
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, X'48656c6c6f');
--directive: reopen
SELECT typeof(payload) FROM t;
